We are living there. Only one elevator is working for the past 10 days. Admin is only available on weekdays 8-12 when all are in office. When in emergency we need to call customer care. With not of button press and waiting. Today the first gate to parking didn't open. Worst ever management K S 75 A building design that doesn't make a lot of sense. This is the first place I moved to that is poorly managed and the developers / contractors have no clue on common sense and what makes sense. "NO ACCESSABLE BUTTONS" There are none on any of the elevator Parking Doors, Garbage Room and especially the Bike Rooms and the Bike Repair Room. This a big No No and will be a big problem. This place advertises accessability. Nothing is easily accessible about this building. They keep one elevator locked off with an Out Of Service sign on it. We moved in and the elevator was unlocked and then relocked end of day. Its probably to monitor that only one elevator is used for moving. "What's with the doors"? The doors are soo heavy and soo hard to open and they slam behind you. They're too spring loaded. Why should my suite door use my strength to hold open until I can quickly get inside or outside before it closes on me. The key lock is black which makes it hard to see where to put the key. The red door is nice but it darkens the keyhole area. The doors open in the wrong direction. You exit the elevator into a small lobby space in parking P1 &P2 and have to pull the heavy n hard to open door that blocks the lobby space and if someone is waiting for the elevator, you have to squish into a corner. If your bringing a little wagon or carrying anything of size, you get stuck in the doorway. The Bike Rooms doors are heavy they should open outwards. That's what Accessable Buttons are for. I struggle with the doors and I've seen others struggle more so for the elderly and families with children. The doors inside the suite doesn't make sense either. The bathroom doors open the wrong way. The main door opens inward so it blocks where you need to stand by part of the sink and fully blocks the drawers from fully opening. The shelf in the shower is in the wrong spot. Its right beside you and when you put things on it its easy to knock them over and you bump into the shelf as you move your arms and turn while washing. I cant put any items on the shelf. The laundry closet space doesn't have a small shelf for your soap. So where do you put it? Well.it goes in the only one small closet for your coats, shoes, and cleaning supplies. Kitchen cupboards are placed up too high to the ceiling. There needs to be a better crown molding than just a curb of the wall. My 6"3 husband cant reach in on the top shelves. There are a couple of drawers that make no sense that are 2 inches deep it's a waste for one decent drawer. I use the dishwasher to store my pots and some pans. What's with soo many light switches? There's 1 light with 3 switches. I could probably sit on my couch with a stick and turn on n off all switches LOL there are 2 switches for each light. And outlets randomly placed everywhere. All the walls have outlets and switches. Craziness. The Garbage room is horrible. Only one big garbage bin for 248 suites (not all sold yet) overflowing and most all floor space is covered with garbage. NO PROPER RECYCLING area.just 3 big bins. One for garbage one for cardboard and one for recycling.and signs over compost with tiny little pics that you can't see what it's showing. Lol, madness. All that is because no cleaners, strata or staff work after 5 or weekends. What part of all this makes sense to you? ? I come from a carpenters family and this is a carpenters nightmare. * For those of you who read this and want to buy, keep all this in mind. results.description: # Newmark Facilitates $83.8 Million Financing for The Deveraux, a Premier Multifamily Property in Denver’s RiNo Neighborhood October 13, 2025 1:00PM October 13, 2025 1:00 PM Newmark announces the Company has facilitated $83.8 million in financing for The Deveraux, a newly constructed, 374-unit trophy multifamily community with 21,000 square feet of Class A retail space located in the vibrant River North (RiNo) neighborhood of Denver, Colorado. The financing was secured through bank lease-up execution on behalf of an undisclosed borrower. Newmark Vice Chairman Lee Redmond and Vice President Nick Schroeder arranged the financing in collaboration with Managing Directors Courtney Crowder and Jack Kachadurian, who provided local market expertise to support the transaction. “The Deveraux’s remarkable leasing success highlights its position as a premier multifamily asset,” said Redmond. “We are proud to have facilitated this significant financing, which reflects the strength of the property and the confidence of the lending community in Denver’s dynamic RiNo neighborhood.” The property, delivered in July 2024, features a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom floor plans averaging 732 square feet. Despite significant supply in the RiNo submarket, The Deveraux has demonstrated exceptional leasing velocity, underscoring its appeal and strong market demand. According to Newmark Research, Denver remains one of the nation’s most active markets for new multifamily deliveries, with elevated completion levels expected to continue through 2025 as the surge of 2021–2022 starts comes online – particularly across urban-core submarkets like RiNo. About Newmark Newmark Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: NMRK), together with its subsidiaries (“Newmark”), is a world leader in commercial real estate, seamlessly powering every phase of the property life cycle. Newmark’s comprehensive suite of services and products is uniquely tailored to each client, from owners to occupiers, investors to founders, and startups to blue-chip companies. Combining the platform’s global reach with market intelligence in both established and emerging property markets, Newmark provides superior service to clients across the industry spectrum. For the twelve months ended June 30, 2025, Newmark generated revenues of over $2.9 billion. As of June 30, 2025, Newmark and its business partners together operated from 165 offices with over 8,400 professionals across four continents. To learn more, visit nmrk.com or follow @newmark. results.description: # Newmark Facilitates $83.8 Million Financing for The Deveraux, a Premier Multifamily Property in Denver’s RiNo Neighborhood October 13, 2025 1:00PM October 13, 2025 1:00 PM Newmark announces the Company has facilitated $83.8 million in financing for The Deveraux, a newly constructed, 374-unit trophy multifamily community with 21,000 square feet of Class A retail space located in the vibrant River North (RiNo) neighborhood of Denver, Colorado. The financing was secured through bank lease-up execution on behalf of an undisclosed borrower. Newmark Vice Chairman Lee Redmond and Vice President Nick Schroeder arranged the financing in collaboration with Managing Directors Courtney Crowder and Jack Kachadurian, who provided local market expertise to support the transaction. “The Deveraux’s remarkable leasing success highlights its position as a premier multifamily asset,” said Redmond. “We are proud to have facilitated this significant financing, which reflects the strength of the property and the confidence of the lending community in Denver’s dynamic RiNo neighborhood.” The property, delivered in July 2024, features a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom floor plans averaging 732 square feet. Despite significant supply in the RiNo submarket, The Deveraux has demonstrated exceptional leasing velocity, underscoring its appeal and strong market demand. The Ayer is a residential high-rise building in Seattle , Washington . The 45-story skyscraper, located in the Denny Triangle neighborhood, was completed in 2023 with 454 luxury apartments and ground-floor retail space.
Design
[ edit ]
The Ayer was designed by Weber Thompson , the same Seattle architecture firm that designed its sister building The Ivey on Boren , as well as nearby towers Stratus and Cirrus . [ 7 ] The 484-foot (148 m) tower features 45 stories above ground and six levels of subterranean parking.
Architectural concept
[ edit ]
The Ayer features a neon artwork titled "Nocturnal Flight" by Seattle artist Yale Wolf, commissioned by Holland Partner Group in collaboration with Urban ArtWorks. [ 15 ] The piece honors Weber Thompson founding partner Blaine Weber (1952–2023), reflecting his "night owl spirit" and love for Seattle.
[ 16 ] Blaine Weber retired in March 2022 after 35 years with the firm and The Ayer was his final Seattle high-rise project. [ 17 ]
Facilities
[ edit ]
Residential
[ edit ]
The Ayer contains 454 apartment units ranging from studios to three-bedroom layouts, with penthouse units on the upper floors. [ 18 ] Units range from 457 to 2,471 sq ft (42.5 to 229.6 m 2 ) . [ 19 ] The residential portion comprises 359,412 sq ft (33,390.5 m 2 ) of the building's total 575,380 sq ft (53,455 m 2 ) .

The Ayer is a residential high-rise building in Seattle , Washington . The 45-story skyscraper, located in the Denny Triangle neighborhood, was completed in 2023 with 454 luxury apartments and ground-floor retail space.
[ edit ]
The Ayer features a neon artwork titled "Nocturnal Flight" by Seattle artist Yale Wolf, commissioned by Holland Partner Group in collaboration with Urban ArtWorks. [ 15 ] The piece honors Weber Thompson founding partner Blaine Weber (1952–2023), reflecting his "night owl spirit" and love for Seattle.
[ 16 ] Blaine Weber retired in March 2022 after 35 years with the firm and The Ayer was his final Seattle high-rise project. [ 17 ]
[ edit ]
The Ayer contains 454 apartment units ranging from studios to three-bedroom layouts, with penthouse units on the upper floors. [ 18 ] Units range from 457 to 2,471 sq ft (42.5 to 229.6 m 2 ) . [ 19 ] The residential portion comprises 359,412 sq ft (33,390.5 m 2 ) of the building's total 575,380 sq ft (53,455 m 2 ) .
[ edit ]
The building has six levels of underground parking with approximately 245–261 stalls, some equipped with electric vehicle charging stations. [ 25 ]
Awards
[ edit ]
The Ayer received the 2024 NAIOP Washington State Night of the Stars award for High-Rise Residential Development of the Year. [ 26 ] [ 27 ]

Thank you for the positive feedback!!
There is only 1 charge per month for trash pick up and that is $15 every month which is also stated in your lease. The additional charge you were seeing was the utility companies initial set up charge and you are only charged that once and never again.
Every month however each resident is charged by the utility company $5.00 for the billing process fee, that is not a charge by Holland or the Alexan. You were also being charged this $5.00 with the prior utility company being NWP.

Kiara (also known as 970 Denny Way) is a residential skyscraper in Seattle , Washington .
The 40-story, 435-foot-tall (133 m) tower has 461 apartments and was completed in 2018. It is first skyscraper in the South Lake Union neighborhood and is one of the few highrise buildings outside the traditional boundaries of Downtown Seattle .
The building is located at the intersection of Denny Way and Terry Avenue, near the headquarters of The Seattle Times and the Cornish College of the Arts . Kiara is owned by Pontegadea , who acquired the building in 2022.

I had an amazing experience living at this location. Not once did I ever feel like my safety was in jeopardy. I was easily able to take a nightly walk around the entire Town & Country complex without a single issue. The common areas are very well maintained.
In my previous apartment I swear the upstairs neighbors wore concrete clogs. The office staff are incredibly friendly. Best of all the mall is right across the river. It's less than a 5 minute walk.
The one time I had the wrong package put in a locker for me, I was able to take it to the correct resident who it turns out had my package, it was a pleasant swap. Second thing is you only get 1 key fob per resident. The fob allows you to enter your apartment.
If you somehow manage to walk out of your apartment without checking to make sure you have the key fob, you will lock yourself out. I unfortunately had a mental episode one time where I forgot to walk out with my fob. There is a $100 charge for them to come open your door should that happen after the office has closed.
If you happen to do it while there is someone in the office then they will happily assist without any charge. That did kinda suck but it was 100% my fault. The good thing is you have an app that can at least get you in the building. If there was 1 thing I could change is to add the ability to open your apartment door to the app.
This is a very nice place to live and you're close to everything you could want to be close to. If the day ever comes that I move back to San Diego, I know what complex I'm going to be looking at first.

results.title: MBK Sells Esperanza at Duarte Station Class A Apartments - Los Angeles Times
results.description:
Irvine-headquartered MBK Rental Living, a developer of apartment communities , announced today that it has successfully executed the sale of its Esperanza at Duarte Station, a 344-unit new transit-oriented Class A apartment community in Duarte, to an undisclosed buyer.
Developed as a joint venture of MBK Rental Living and Haseko Corporation, Esperanza reflects the persistent demand for high‑quality, amenity‑rich communities that align with what today’s residents value most in their living experience.
“At MBK Rental Living, we believe great communities are built around people, not just buildings.
Esperanza at Duarte Station brings that belief to life through intentional design, dynamic rooftop amenities, inviting courtyards, and immersive, year-round resident programming.
The result is more than a place to live – it’s a lifestyle that fosters connection, energy, and a true sense of belonging,” said Ken McCarren, president of MBK Rental Living. “The community’s proximity to the Metro station and the world‑renowned City of Hope makes it especially attractive for those seeking connection, opportunity, and ease.
We are seeing this same strong demand at Solana at Duarte Station, reinforcing the long-term appeal of this exceptional market.”
Opened in November 2022, Esperanza at Duarte Station is a five-story community with a total of 344 studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartments ranging from 514 to 1,090 square feet with 56 different floor plans.
It is located on a 4.3-acre property at the intersection of Highland Avenue and Fasana Road.
Advertisement
Esperanza is highlighted with rooftop amenities offering dramatic views of the San Gabriel mountains, including a resort-style pool and spa; an indoor/outdoor casita with a living room lounge, fireplace, open dining room and entertainers-style kitchen; a landscaped roof deck with poolside cabanas, outdoor TVs with bar, grilling stations, fire pit
and lounge area; and a rooftop gym with free weights, cardio and HIIT zones and outdoor yoga.
The community’s first-level amenities include a co-working area with open seating, a cantina with lounge and counter seating with direct access to a “food truck alley, and the popular “Casa de Perro” with an interior pet wash and dry station as well as an exterior dog park with seating.
Esperanza is within walking distance of the Duarte/City of Hope Metro Gold Line commuter train station, and City of Hope, a 120-acre comprehensive cancer treatment center and major area employer. The train and freeway access eases transit to nearby Los Angeles, Pasadena and other Southern California business and entertainment destinations.
In addition to Esperanza, MBK Rental Living is currently leasing Southern California communities at Solana at Duarte Station and Zia in Anaheim . The company also has several active communities in Northern California and Colorado.

results.title: MBK Sells Esperanza at Duarte Station Class A Apartments - Los Angeles Times
results.description:
Irvine-headquartered MBK Rental Living, a developer of apartment communities , announced today that it has successfully executed the sale of its Esperanza at Duarte Station, a 344-unit new transit-oriented Class A apartment community in Duarte, to an undisclosed buyer.
Developed as a joint venture of MBK Rental Living and Haseko Corporation, Esperanza reflects the persistent demand for high‑quality, amenity‑rich communities that align with what today’s residents value most in their living experience.
“At MBK Rental Living, we believe great communities are built around people, not just buildings.
Esperanza at Duarte Station brings that belief to life through intentional design, dynamic rooftop amenities, inviting courtyards, and immersive, year-round resident programming.
The result is more than a place to live – it’s a lifestyle that fosters connection, energy, and a true sense of belonging,” said Ken McCarren, president of MBK Rental Living. “The community’s proximity to the Metro station and the world‑renowned City of Hope makes it especially attractive for those seeking connection, opportunity, and ease.
We are seeing this same strong demand at Solana at Duarte Station, reinforcing the long-term appeal of this exceptional market.”
Opened in November 2022, Esperanza at Duarte Station is a five-story community with a total of 344 studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartments ranging from 514 to 1,090 square feet with 56 different floor plans.
It is located on a 4.3-acre property at the intersection of Highland Avenue and Fasana Road.
Advertisement
Esperanza is highlighted with rooftop amenities offering dramatic views of the San Gabriel mountains, including a resort-style pool and spa; an indoor/outdoor casita with a living room lounge, fireplace, open dining room and entertainers-style kitchen; a landscaped roof deck with poolside cabanas, outdoor TVs with bar, grilling stations, fire pit
and lounge area; and a rooftop gym with free weights, cardio and HIIT zones and outdoor yoga.
The community’s first-level amenities include a co-working area with open seating, a cantina with lounge and counter seating with direct access to a “food truck alley, and the popular “Casa de Perro” with an interior pet wash and dry station as well as an exterior dog park with seating.
Esperanza is within walking distance of the Duarte/City of Hope Metro Gold Line commuter train station, and City of Hope, a 120-acre comprehensive cancer treatment center and major area employer. The train and freeway access eases transit to nearby Los Angeles, Pasadena and other Southern California business and entertainment destinations.
In addition to Esperanza, MBK Rental Living is currently leasing Southern California communities at Solana at Duarte Station and Zia in Anaheim . The company also has several active communities in Northern California and Colorado.
Information for this article was sourced from MBK Rental Living .

My wife and I have lived at The Preserve at Cedar River to nearly two years now. Our experience has been outstanding. First and foremost, management is outstanding.
This, of course, is not the fault of The Preserve, but it *is* worth noting about the lights and the way they react to undisciplined and irresponsible upstairs neighbors. The apartment complex is well maintained, from lighting to grounds-keeping.
right away. The maintenance staff is friendly and helpful, quick to respond to issues. On the rare occasions when a problem arises, maintenance shows up the next day and takes care of the problem thoroughly. As a bonus, this is close to the Cedar River and Cedar River Trail.
This is great for jogging and bicycling, and if you enjoy river tubing there is a perfect spot just outside the apartment's back gate for jumping in and drifting downstream to nearby Carco Theater and park. We love this annual ritual, with late July being the perfect time for warm water and low (but not too low) levels.
I do NOT recommend parking at the nearby Ron Regis Park, where there are athletic facilities. The one time I parked there my car was vandalized and my valuables were stolen. Renton Landing, about a five to ten minute drive west, has plenty of entertainment to choose from--a cinema, lots of food options, and shopping.
In summation, I highly recommend this apartment. It is the best apartment in which we have lived, and aside from noisy neighbors, better than the house from which we moved. What are you waiting for? Move in!

Sections 8.22.500 of the Oakland Municipal Code is amended as set forth below (additions are shown as double underline and deletions are shown as strikethrough).
8.22.500 Rent program service fee.
A. Establishment of the Fee. The rent program service fee (the "fee") is hereby established.
The fee is to be charged against any residential rental unit that is subject to either the Rent Adjustment Ordinance, the Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance, or both.
B. Definitions.
The fee is to be charged on a per unit basis against all residential rental units that are either covered units or are covered by the Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance, except such residential rental units that are owned or operated by a public entity, including, but not limited to, the City of Oakland, the Redevelopment Agency of the City of
Oakland, and the Oakland Housing Authority. A rental property owner who does not timely pay the fee because the rental property owner claims the dwelling unit is not subject to the fee must pay all fees, delinquent charges, interest, and collection costs for any dwelling unit that is found by the city to be subject to the fee.
A rental property owner who has not paid the fee and any charges related to a delinquency in payment of the fee cannot:
1. Respond to a petition brought by a tenant; or
2. Petition for a rent increase.
I. Delinquent Charges, Interest, and Collection Costs.
3. An owner who does not pay the fee on or before the date it is considered late must pay a delinquency charge according to the following schedule:
a.
In addition to the delinquent charges, a rental property owner who fails to remit the fee due by the date it is late shall pay simple interest at the rate of one percent per month or fraction thereof on the amount of the fee inclusive of delinquent charges from the date the fee is late.
4.
The amount of any fee, delinquent charges, interest, and collection costs imposed by Chapter 8.22 shall be deemed a debt to the city and any rental property owner carrying on a residential rental business without paying the fee and/or any delinquent charges, interest or collection costs shall be liable in an action in the name of the city in any
the amount of the fee and any tax and delinquent charges, interest or
collection costs imposed. An action to collect the fee must be commenced

One of the many mid-rise modern apartment buildings in South Lake Union. Lived here for a couple years.
Nice location, close to the lake, Queen Anne, Seattle Center, downtown, public transportation, and offices of the various companies in SLU.
They are in the middle in terms of the more modern apartment complexes in the area. Not as nice as the more expensive high rises, but better finishes for places nearby that are cheaper.
Has electronic access via key fobs, and the apartment door keys are electronic. Facilities like lounge and fitness center are on the smaller side, but functional. Noise insulation seems good, but maybe it's because I lived on the top floor sharing only one wall with another unit.
Maintenance has been prompt and the common areas are cleaned regularly. The office staff has changed a few times during my stay, but I found them to be pleasant. There are resident events, but as with most apartments they tend to decrease in frequency as the building gets older.
There are also the general noise and homeless issues with areas surrounding downtown Seattle. Also there is no AC in the apartments, and it can get pretty hot in the summers especially with heat waves in the last few years.
I stayed a couple of years because it was a convenient location, close to work. Moved out when my workplace moved.
Move out was smooth. They charged the cleaning fee I was expecting and that was that.

About JUXT
JUXT stands out as an exceptional apartment community in Seattle, characterized by its modern design and sophisticated finishes that create a sleek and inviting atmosphere. The building features spacious units flooded with natural light, providing residents with a comfortable and stylish living environment.
JUXT offers an impressive array of amenities, including a well-equipped gym, a cozy speakeasy, and a rooftop lounge that boasts stunning views of the city and the nearby lake. These features cater to a diverse lifestyle, making it an ideal choice for anyone seeking both comfort and convenience in urban living.
The location of JUXT enhances its appeal, situated close to major tech companies like Amazon, Meta, and Google, along with an abundance of restaurants and cafes that make daily errands a breeze. Residents appreciate the building's commitment to cleanliness and maintenance, with staff consistently praised for their responsiveness and helpfulness.
With controlled key entry, ample package storage, and a strong sense of community, JUXT not only prioritizes security but also fosters a friendly environment. This apartment community is truly a gem for those looking for a vibrant yet comfortable lifestyle in Seattle.

Formerly called The District by Windsor, 6300 E Hampden Avenue, The District at Hampden South was sold by GID, a real estate company based in Boston, to Mesirow Financial , a Chicago-based financial services firm, according to a Tuesday news release from JLL Capital Markets.
“The sale of The District by Windsor demonstrates the continued investor appetite for well-located, value-add multi-housing assets in the Denver metro area,” said Jordan Robbins, senior managing director at JLL, in the news release.
Constructed in 2007, the mid-rise apartment community is situated on a 7-acre plot and features nearly 250,000 square feet of residential space, complemented by 16,622 square feet of commercial space.
With over 60 years of experience, GID manages $30 billion in assets as of Sept. 30, including 57,000 apartment units and 28 million square feet of industrial and commercial space while also offering commercial real estate debt solutions through its credit platform.
With a 95% occupancy rate, The District has 276 units, featuring a selection of studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments, based on their website.
Each unit is equipped with 9-foot ceilings, gourmet kitchens with stainless steel appliances and dark cherry wood or maple cabinetry.

By Jessica Alvarado Gamez | jalvarado@denverpost.com
PUBLISHED: January 15, 2025 at 11:47 AM MST | UPDATED: January 15, 2025 at 2:18 PM MST
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
A three-building multi-housing community in Denver’s Hampden South neighborhood has been sold for $91.1 million, according to the city’s Assessor’s Office.
Formerly called The District by Windsor, 6300 E Hampden Avenue, The District at Hampden South was sold by GID, a real estate company based in Boston, to Mesirow Financial , a Chicago-based financial services firm, according to a Tuesday news release from JLL Capital Markets.
“The sale of The District by Windsor demonstrates the continued investor appetite for well-located, value-add multi-housing assets in the Denver metro area,” said Jordan Robbins, senior managing director at JLL, in the news release.
With a 95% occupancy rate, The District has 276 units, featuring a selection of studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments, based on their website.
Each unit is equipped with 9-foot ceilings, gourmet kitchens with stainless steel appliances and dark cherry wood or maple cabinetry.
Select apartments feature 20-foot cathedral ceilings and gas fireplaces.
The property also provides a range of amenities, including a year-round spa and hot tub, a resort-style swimming pool, a 24-hour fitness center, a resident clubroom and EV charging stations.

SAN JOSE — A San Jose apartment complex near the city’s mega malls has been bought for just over $100 million, but the property’s price has barely budged since the last time it traded hands.
Meridian at Midtown, a 218-unit residential hub, was purchased for $105.3 million, documents filed on June 24 with the Santa Clara County Recorder’s Office show.

The latest price for the west San Jose apartment complex , located at 1432 West San Carlos St.

Essex Property Trust was the seller in the deal.
In 2018, Essex Property paid $104 million for the Meridian at Midtown apartments, according to county real estate files.

The Ivey on Boren offers an exquisite blend of modern luxury and artistic design in the heart of Seattle’s Belltown. Residents are treated to a wealth of amenities such as an elegant pool, relaxing hot tub, and a state-of-the-art gym, all of which contribute to a serene and fulfilling lifestyle.
The property is especially praised for its responsive and professional leasing team, which enhances the community's welcoming vibe. With the Cornish College of the Arts auditorium and gallery right on site, the artistic essence is palpable, offering residents a true cultural retreat.
Cats and dogs are allowed, ensuring your furry friends feel right at home. Nestled in a convenient location, it provides easy access to essentials and entertainment, making urban living both comfortable and enriching.

About Coen & Columbia
Coen & Columbia stands out as an exceptional residential community that combines modern design with a vibrant urban lifestyle. Renowned for its beautiful interiors and high-quality finishes, each apartment reflects a commitment to excellence and comfort, making it a desirable choice for anyone seeking a stylish living environment.
The building boasts outstanding amenities, including a well-appointed gym and community lounge, fostering a sense of community among residents. With a location that provides easy access to restaurants, bars, and waterfront parks, Coen & Columbia offers the perfect blend of convenience and leisure.
The building's thoughtful construction features thick walls that contribute to a near soundproof experience, enhancing the overall quality of life. The dedicated and friendly staff are frequently noted for their responsiveness and willingness to assist, creating a welcoming atmosphere for all residents.
Additionally, regular community events help build connections among tenants, making this a special place to call home. The surrounding neighborhood is rich with activities, from farmers markets to scenic waterfront walks, ensuring that residents can enjoy a dynamic lifestyle right at their doorstep.
Coen & Columbia not only represents a modern living space but also embodies a community spirit that resonates deeply with those who choose to reside there.

Amenities and More
Customer experiences highlight several appealing aspects of Coen & Columbia living.
Review highlights: • Residents value the exceptional responsiveness and warmth of the management team, particularly praising staff members like Ryan, Hilary, and Darren for their consistent support and community engagement.
• The location receives high marks for convenience, with reviewers noting easy access to parks, dining options, waterfront areas, and local businesses, making daily errands and leisure activities effortless.
• Many commend the thoughtfully designed interiors featuring quality finishes, ample natural light, and functional layouts that enhance everyday comfort, along with pet-friendly policies appreciated by animal owners.
Additional feedback: Some residents point out periodic noise issues from neighboring units and the parking garage, which occasionally disrupt daily life despite management's efforts to address concerns promptly.
Collectively, these elements create a well-regarded urban living experience suited for those seeking walkable neighborhoods and active community involvement in downtown Vancouver.

Rooted in the authentic nature of San Diego, The Torrey is downtown San Diego’s newest luxury apartment community and a true reflection of elevated coastal living.
Rooted in the authentic nature of San Diego, The Torrey is downtown San Diego’s newest luxury apartment community and a true reflection of elevated coastal living.
Studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartments and penthouse residences arrive in light and dark designer finishes, with floor-to-ceiling windows, quartz countertops, and open layouts designed to maximize light and connection to the city around you. Daily life at The Torrey unfolds across spaces designed for both connection and escape.
Above it all on the 34th floor, The Canopy provides sweeping city views from an elegant indoor lounge, and The Nest sets the stage for an evening around the fire of an open-air rooftop terrace, steps from the rooftop pool and spa overlooking the San Diego Bay.
Residents will also enjoy the convenience of a Whole Foods Market opening on the ground floor of The Torrey delivering prior to the end of 2026.
Positioned in the heart of downtown San Diego, The Torrey puts Little Italy at your doorstep, home to Little Italy Mercato, San Diego’s largest farmers market, and chef-driven restaurants, such as Herb & Wood and Kettner Exchange.
Additionally, The Torrey is conveniently located 1 mile from the Embarcadero waterfront, Seaport Village, and Gaslamp Quarter. Commuting is effortless with quick access to 1-5, 1-163, and Santa Fe Depot, while San Diego International Airport is just 2 miles away.

results.title: Vicino on the Lake | Frequently Asked Questions
results.description:
Why do your prices have ranges?
Our apartment homes are priced based on classic or updated features.
What is the application fee and is it refundable?
Application fees are $75 per person for everyone 18 years or older that will be occupying the apartment. You may pay these online by credit card (a small fee will apply). All application fees are non-refundable.
What is the hold fee and is it refundable?
A one-time non-refundable Holding Fee of $100 is due at the time of application, and will hold the apartment off the market while we process your application.
What is the administrative fee and is it refundable?
The administrative fee is a non-refundable $100 fee that is due at move in.
How do I apply?
Applications may be found under the log in tab of our property website, or you can stop in the office for a paper application during business hours.
Which utilities do I pay?
Residents are responsible for paying their own gas and electric bills through Ameren and Spire. The resident is also responsible for a portion of water and sewer, in addition to your base monthly rent. If you fail to have utilities in your name during your occupancy, you will be billed $50 and the cost of the utility.
What is the security deposit?
Security deposits will vary depending on qualifying criteria. Security deposits start at $300 and go up from there.
When is my rent payment due? What day of the month am I liable for a late charge?
Rent is always due on the first of the month and a $75 late fee is assessed on the 6th of every month (Sundays and holidays included). An additional $5 a day is assessed after the 6th until rent is paid in full.
What kind of pets do you allow? How many pets may I have?
A non-refundable pet fee of $325 for 1 pet and $425 for 2 pets is due at move in, plus a monthly pet fee of $40 per 1 pet and $50 for 2 pets is required at move in.  A non-refundable Doggie DNA fee of $50 is required per pet at move in. ???? A maximum of two (2) pets per apartment, with a combined weight limit of 100 pounds, no breed restrictions.
Resident Questions
If I am part of the military and receive deployment or reassignment orders, can I break the lease?
Yes, if the lease break fee has been paid. A 60-day notice is required before vacating your apartment, and the lease break fee is $2500. Please make sure that you reference your signed lease agreement and confirm policies with your Property Manager as there could be unique circumstances.
Your guests are welcome at Vicino. If someone is temporarily staying with you, please let the office know so we can accommodate for parking. If someone is permanently moving in, or staying longer than 14 days, they will need to fill out an application to be added to your lease agreement.
I will be moving out. What do I need to do?
Vicino on the Lake Apartments must be listed as an additional interested party or interested party on your renter's insurance policy:
Vicino on the Lake Apartments PO Box 498067 Cincinnati, OH 45249

About The Rodney
The Rodney stands out as an exemplary residential community located in the vibrant Pearl District of Portland, Oregon. With its modern architecture and luxurious amenities, this building appeals to those seeking a comfortable urban lifestyle.
Residents rave about the impressive rooftop views that offer a breathtaking panorama of the city skyline, perfect for hosting gatherings or enjoying serene sunsets.
The attentive management team is consistently highlighted for their dedication to creating a welcoming environment; they promptly address resident concerns and ensure that communal spaces are well-maintained. Notably, individuals appreciate the soundproof apartments designed for tranquility amidst city living.
Key features include secure parking options and pet-friendly policies, which add convenience and peace of mind for residents with furry companions. The apartment interiors boast contemporary designs with ample storage space, high-quality appliances, and inviting layouts—ideal for both relaxation and entertaining guests.
Moreover, responsive maintenance staff further enhances living conditions by swiftly resolving issues when they arise. While challenges like cleanliness in common areas have been noted due to increasing foot traffic from nearby developments, overall sentiments lean towards satisfaction with life at The Rodney.
This property offers not only quality living spaces but also fosters a genuine sense of community among its residents through professional service and warmth.

I looked at the property and the unit was beautiful with a gorgeous view; and figured I could overlook the reeking smell of pot all throughout the building during my tour. I decided that night to put a $500 deposit on a unit.
The contract clearly says you lock in your price at the time of deposit and the contract says when Holland/agents are required to have the unit ready by. The next morning the sales rep called and said “thanks for all your documents and credit check authorization etc.
however, it’ll take another 3-5 days on our end to process your pay stubs so I sent you a price chart of how much it will go up over the next few days. If we can process it in 3 days, it’ll only go up by $30 per month, but it may be $45-$50 if it takes 5 days.” What? How is this my problem?
The contract I signed on May 14 says you need to have the unit ready for me to move in on May 15. “Well, no it doesn’t work that way…” No. I don’t do business that way. I’m out per the contract and have 72 hours to leave and get my deposit back.
(Minus the $55 application fee.) So here it is…May 30 and I haven’t received my $500 deposit back after dealing with 2 sales reps and the Corporate Office. Avoid this place like the plague. Please.

We have only just moved in but I am already impressed with Palladia. Upon move in inspection we found a few issues and they were addressed immediately. The maintenance was efficient and friendly. I have not had any issues with parking this week and usually have gotten a spot right in front of our apartment.
First and foremost, Palladia is the Worst place I have ever lived. They will do anything to nickel and dime you and then completely ignore your concerns. Prior to moving out, we contacted management to set up a move-out inspection, which Palladia encouraged, but they refused due to Covid.
We offered to go stand outside the unit while they did the inspection and they declined, but a couple weeks prior, they had no issue sending maintenance into our unit while our entire family was inside, unmasked. Palladia states their carpet has a lifespan of 60 months. Upon us moving out, our carpet had been used 58 months.
Management said they were keeping our entire deposit and then charging us an additional $200 on top of that to replace the carpet due to excessive pet urine despite us NOT ever having a pet.
I told them that the urine HAD to be there prior to us moving in, which was gross. I finally told management I would be contacting their corporate offices due to the matter and Palladia finally agreed we were not responsible for the cost of carpet replacement and returned our deposit.
But since WSG is a month or two behind, part of your deposit will automatically be taken and applied toward that.
Be prepared to leave your unit cleaner than when you first moved in.
Stove, refrigerator and washer and dryer were surrounded by dust, dirt and other debris, which was not a huge problem as I usually do light cleaning prior to moving in somewhere.
Furthermore, four days after moving in, I submitted my first noise complaint due to 4 straight nights of excessive noise between Midnight and 4AM. I expect noise living in an apartment, but this was beyond excessive.
In addition, police are called to this apartment complex monthly.
Do yourself a favor and stay away from this place.

UserWay icon for accessibility widget
True North Apartments are located on 801 Dexter Avenue North, Seattle, WA. (Image: Joshua Lewis / Seattle Refined) True North Apartments are located on 801 Dexter Avenue North, Seattle, WA.
(Image: Joshua Lewis / Seattle Refined) True North Apartments are located on 801 Dexter Avenue North, Seattle, WA. (Image: Joshua Lewis / Seattle Refined) 22 View all photos
If you feel most at home scaling a snow-covered mountain, exploring a rocky trail or kayaking in pristine waters, True North is calling.
Seattle's newest apartment complex in South Lake Union is officially opening its doors this weekend, but you might completely forget that you're indoors when you set foot in this haven for outdoor enthusiasts. It's about as close as you'll come to permanently living in the great outdoors, while still enjoying all the comforts of home.
True North is unlike any of the ultra-modern residences sprouting up in the rapidly growing SLU neighborhood. It is the only apartment community in Seattle with a bouldering wall (yep, I said a bouldering wall) for residents who want to take their first baby rock climbing steps, or to hone serious climbing skills.
The configuration will be changing every few months, so climbers will be continually challenged.
After being stuck in a cubicle all day, reconnecting with nature is as easy as borrowing one of True North's two kayaks, unplugging, and taking a paddle around Lake Union.
Got the itch to explore?
The Trailhead Room at True North can help you chart out your next great expedition. It is the centerpiece of the community featuring a map of Mt. Rainier. A library of maps and books will point you in the direction of your own personal Everest.
True North can even help you gear up for an adventure thanks to a partnership with the gear rental company Back40 Outfitters .
Some of the other unique features include a gear storage area (sadly, all adventures must come to an end).
It feels more like a lounge with pinball machines, couches and lockers that provide a home for all of your outdoor toys. There's even a place to dry out your camping equipment and wax skis and snowboards.
Expansive outdoor terraces mark the perfect place to trade tales of wild adventures while grilling, swinging on a hammock or making a pizza in the outdoor pizza oven.
Let's not forget about the apartments, they have Mother Nature in mind, too!
True North boasts energy and water efficient appliances, recycled materials (when possible), and they promise to plant a tree for every lease signed to help reforest and preserve Seattle parks.
